question: What does the pair a push makes cost — one signed append, then the read the next push is served from — and does the cost of charging still rise with the record?

build.note: A/B between the two BUILT trees: only the compiled files were swapped, dist deleted and rebuilt for each arm.

protocol.order: ALTERNATED — base, branch, branch, base — so a term that is only fast because of where it sits in the run shows as a gap between the two placings of the same arm.

protocol.reads_measured: listDecisionsByState through the session cache registry — the term a write destroys, not the whole hook.

amplification.question: 211 charges in a row, each an append plus the read the next one is served from. Does the per-charge median rise as the record grows?
amplification.reading: Every arm grew the chain by exactly 241947 bytes, so the arms did identical work. On the base the median rises 38-45% along the run; on the branch it does not rise.
